title: Fluctuating fatigue
summary: Woman in her 40s with relapsing-remitting MS whose fatigue and hand numbness come and go. Her PIP2 describes good days; an MS nurse fatigue diary (Jul-Sep 2026) gives approximate counts of bad days, so most activities turn on the reg 7 share of days, and preparing food only scores by combining two descriptors under reg 7(1)(c). Walking turns on whether she can manage the distance repeatedly.

conditions_in_documents: Intermittent numbness / reduced sensation in both hands

must_find.quote: Some days I am too tired and we have something easy or he helps.
Bad fatigue days son does the chopping, lifting pans, draining pasta.
Numb hands days (energy ok) won't use the hob — dropped a pan of boiling water in June, scalded her foot slightly.
This gives a picture of bad fatigue days on around 4 days in 10
Roughly half of the days with hand numbness were also bad fatigue days.

gaps: Diary counts are approximate and some August days were missed; the combined share (about 55%) is close to 50%, so a firmer count would help
The overlap between numbness days and fatigue days is given only as 'roughly half', so the number of numbness-only days is an estimate
No statement from the son about what he does on bad days
Form does not mention the hob/safety issue on numbness days
activities.draft_note: Neither alone is over 50%, but 1e (bad fatigue days, ~39/92) plus 1c (numbness-only days, ~12/92) is about 55%, so reg 7(1)(c) gives 1e as the more frequent: 4 points.

must_find.quote: When hands numb son sometimes cuts up meat for her. CL says "only now and then", couldn't say how often.

gaps: Form says 'No problems'; no frequency for help cutting food
Unclear whether this only happens on numbness days (about 26% of days) or less often
activities.draft_note: 2b(iii) assistance to cut up food happens sometimes, but nothing suggests over 50% of days; frequency needed.
Self-manages medication with a phone alarm; all documents agree.

must_find.quote: I have a stool in the shower so I can sit.
uses the shower stool supplied by OT in 2025, as she cannot stand for the length of a shower on any day
Washing: always sits on OT shower stool, has done since 2025.

gaps: Does not use the bath; no evidence on whether she could get in or out of an unadapted bath
activities.draft_note: Needs a shower stool to wash on every day: 4b, 2 points.
Mild urgency only, no accidents and no help needed; no difficulty with the activity.

must_find.quote: I can dress myself, it just takes me longer.
Worst days son helps with socks and shoes, CL estimates 4-5 days a month.
On bad fatigue days dresses sitting on bed, "takes forever", rests between items. Couldn't give time.
On those days she reports dropping things and difficulty with buttons, zips and handling hot pans.

gaps: No time given for dressing on bad days, so the reasonable time period test cannot be applied yet
Help with socks and shoes (6d) is about 4-5 days a month, well under 50%
Unclear whether sitting on the bed to dress is needed (possible aid) or a preference
Pull-on clothing and front-fastening bra on numbness days: whether this amounts to an aid is for the reviewer
activities.draft_note: Help on some days, not most: 6d only about 15% of days; reasonable time on bad fatigue days (~42%) is untested until a dressing-time diary exists.
No difficulty reported in any document.
Reading glasses only, which do not count for 8b.
No difficulty reported; past low mood resolved.
Manages own bills; slower on bad days but no help needed.
Not going out on bad days is due to physical fatigue, not psychological distress or difficulty following a route.

must_find.quote: I can walk to the shop at the end of the road. My legs get heavy if I go too far.
On a good day she can walk around 200 to 300 metres at a steady pace.
On bad days she reports needing to stop after about 50 metres because her legs feel heavy.
Asked could she walk back and then do it again later — "no chance, I'd be done for the day".
Said after the shop walk she usually has to sit on the wall outside before walking back.

gaps: Distance to the shop is not measured (only 'about 5 mins')
Specialist distances are self-reported, not observed
Whether she can walk over 200 metres repeatedly on good days is the deciding question and is not yet answered
Bad-day figure of 'about 50 metres' sits on the 12b/12c boundary
activities.draft_note: Bad days (~42%) suggest 12b or 12c, under 50% alone; it scores only if good-day walking over 200m fails the repeatedly test, which needs evidence.

must_not_claim: That she uses a walking stick or any other walking aid
A measured walking distance or a measured dressing time
That she has bladder or bowel incontinence
That she has anxiety or depression affecting going out or engaging with people
That her son helps her wash or dress her upper body
A specific number of days a month on which her son cuts up her food
